children: Shares of Viking Therapeutics fell after the biopharmaceutical company said it plans to offer $200 million each of common stock and convertible senior notes due 2032.
Shares fell 8.2% to $38.24 in after-hours trading on Wednesday. The stock closed up 2% at $41.65, up 18% this year.
The company said that the underwriters of each offering will have 30-day options to buy up to an additional $30 million worth of both the shares and notes.
The notes in the offering mature on Oct. 15, 2032.

The company said it plans to use proceeds from the offering to support the clinical development and advancement of its VK2735 and VK3019 programs, as well as for other general research and development and general corporate purposes.
